objective: Standard statement: for a three-fold space H with a minimal map of genus g and the 4^g spin structures q (quadratic forms on H_1), let N_q(B) and N_q(B - L) be the q-signed even-subgraph sums of the incidence graph (and of it minus a contact L) at the knot's coupling i/sqrt(3), normalized; (1) spin sum: #col(H) = 2^-g sum_q (-1)^Arf(q) N_q(B) and #col(H - L) = 2^-g sum_q (-1)^Arf(q) N_q(B - L), so non-colourability is the balance of even and odd sectors; (2) of the 4^g Kasteleyn sign classes of a minimal map, the knot's is the only one that is not 2-colourable; (3) on the Fano torus the sectors are 8, 8, 8 | 24 (closed) and 16, 16, 16 | 28 (one contact opened) on every map and contact: the amplitude is not carried by the even spin structures and the odd one does not cancel; (4) on the 13-point space the sector matrices indexed by the two handles' spin structures have full rank: the sectors do not factor over handles. Nearest known result: Kac-Ward and Fisher; Cimasoni (generalized Kac-Ward formula); Loebl-Masbaum (Arf invariant formula); THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE-20261030-001C. Classification: to be decided.
status: Proved: the knot's colouring counts are Arf-signed sums of spin sectors; non-colourability is the balance of even and odd sectors; the knot's sign class is the only non-colourable Kasteleyn class; on the Fano torus every sector contributes (8,8,8|24 closed, 16,16,16|28 opened), so 5 per handle does not come from the even spin structures alone; at genus 2 the sectors do not factor over handles
title: Spin sectors of the knot's count
